title: Registration
outcomes: Compute aggregate turnover and test the threshold.
Identify persons not liable and those who must register.
Apply the procedure, effective date and special persons rules.

meta.exam_tip: Check section 24 first — if it applies, the threshold is irrelevant.

concepts.title: Threshold and aggregate turnover (s. 22)
body: Section 22: every supplier making taxable supplies must register in the State or UT from where he makes them if aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura).
For persons exclusively supplying goods, the limit is ₹40 lakh in most States (excluding a few special category States and notified goods such as ice cream, pan masala and tobacco).

Aggregate turnover (s. 2(6)): taxable supplies, exempt supplies, exports and inter-State supplies of all persons with the same PAN across India — excluding inward supplies taxed under reverse charge and the GST itself. A person taking over a business of a registered person is liable from the date of transfer.
concepts.analogy: The threshold is tested on all-India turnover under one PAN, but registration is State-wise.
concepts.work: A consultant with ₹15 lakh taxable and ₹8 lakh exempt services must register — exempt turnover counts.

concepts.title: Persons not liable (s. 23) and compulsory registration (s. 24)
body: Section 23: not liable — persons exclusively supplying non-taxable or wholly exempt goods or services; agriculturists supplying produce from cultivation; and notified categories (persons making only reverse-charge supplies, inter-State service suppliers within the threshold, inter-State handicraft suppliers within the threshold, small suppliers of goods through e-commerce subject to conditions).

Section 24: registration irrespective of turnover for inter-State taxable supply of goods; casual taxable persons; persons liable under reverse charge; ECOs liable under section 9(5); non-resident taxable persons; TDS deductors under section 51; agents supplying on behalf of others; input service distributors; persons supplying through ECOs that collect TCS (subject to exemptions); every ECO required to collect TCS; and suppliers of online information and database access services from outside India to unregistered persons in India.
concepts.analogy: Some activities are risky enough that the law demands registration from the first rupee.
concepts.work: A ₹5 lakh trader who sells goods once to a buyer in another State must register.

concepts.title: Procedure, special persons and effective date (ss. 25–27)
body: Section 25: apply within 30 days of becoming liable, in each State or UT where liable; a coastal supplier registers in the nearest State. A person may take separate registrations for each place of business in a State. Registration is PAN-based, with Aadhaar authentication or biometric verification. Voluntary registration is permitted; UN bodies and embassies get a Unique Identity Number.

Casual and non-resident taxable persons apply at least 5 days before starting business; registration is valid for the period stated or 90 days (extendable by 90 days), and an advance deposit of estimated tax is required.

Section 27 and Rule 10: effective date is the date of liability if applied within 30 days; otherwise the date of grant. A simplified, faster registration (Rule 14A) is available to small suppliers whose monthly output tax does not exceed ₹2.5 lakh.
concepts.analogy: Register within 30 days and the registration reaches back to the day liability began.
concepts.work: Liable on 1 May, applied on 20 May, granted on 1 June: effective date is 1 May.

concepts.title: Amendment, cancellation and revocation (ss. 28–30)
body: Section 28: core fields (legal name, address of principal place, additional places, partners or directors) need the officer's approval; other fields are amended online; a change in PAN needs fresh registration.

Section 29: the person may seek cancellation on discontinuance, transfer of business, change in constitution or no longer being liable. The officer may cancel for contravention, non-filing of returns (six continuous months; a financial year plus three months for composition), not starting business within six months of voluntary registration, or fraud. Cancellation can be retrospective; tax on stock and capital goods (ITC or tax on transaction value, whichever is higher) must be paid.
Section 30: revocation may be sought within 90 days of the cancellation order (extendable up to 180 days more) after filing pending returns and paying dues.
concepts.analogy: Registration can be changed, surrendered or taken away — and, if taken away, often restored on compliance.
concepts.work: A trader whose registration was cancelled for non-filing can apply for revocation after filing all returns.

illustrations.title: Is registration needed?
illustrations.q: Mr. Joseph of Kochi, Kerala, supplies services. In the year: taxable intra-State services ₹12 lakh; exempt services ₹3 lakh; export of services ₹2.5 lakh; taxable services from his Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu) branch under the same PAN ₹4 lakh; inward supplies on which he paid tax under reverse charge ₹1.5 lakh; GST collected ₹2.88 lakh. Is he liable to register?

solution.text: ₹21.5 lakh exceeds ₹20 lakh, so he must register in Kerala and in Tamil Nadu (each State where he makes taxable supplies) within 30 days.

illustrations.title: Compulsory or not?
illustrations.q: Turnover of each person below is ₹8 lakh. Who must register? (a) A trader of garments making one inter-State sale of goods; (b) a person selling only handicraft goods inter-State; (c) a company paying reverse charge on legal fees; (d) a farmer selling his own wheat; (e) a person who comes to a Mumbai trade fair for 10 days and sells goods there.

jobs.title: New client registration
jobs.situation: A start-up expects to cross ₹20 lakh in its first year and will sell online across India.
steps: Check section 24 triggers such as inter-State goods and ECO sales.
Collect PAN, Aadhaar, address proof and bank details.
Apply in each State with a place of business.
Calendar the effective date for invoicing.
jobs.takeaway: Section 24 often makes registration necessary long before the turnover threshold.

mcqs.q: Registration threshold for a service provider in Gujarat:
mcqs.explain: Service providers outside the four States with a ₹10 lakh limit have a ₹20 lakh threshold. ₹40 lakh is for exclusive goods suppliers. In practice: count all-India turnover under the PAN.

options: Inward supplies on which tax is paid under reverse charge
mcqs.explain: Reverse charge inward supplies and GST are excluded; exempt, export and inter-branch supplies are included. In practice: watch exempt turnover.

mcqs.q: Which person is NOT required to register?
options: An agriculturist selling produce from his own cultivation
mcqs.explain: Section 23 exempts agriculturists for produce from cultivation; the others are in section 24. In practice: a farmer who trades in others' produce is not covered.
mcqs.topic: Persons not liable (s. 23) and compulsory registration (s. 24)

mcqs.q: Registration must be applied for within how many days of becoming liable?
mcqs.explain: Section 25(1) gives 30 days; casual and non-resident persons apply 5 days before business. In practice: late application shifts the effective date.
mcqs.topic: Procedure, special persons and effective date (ss. 25–27)

mcqs.q: A casual taxable person's registration is valid for:
options: The period specified or 90 days, extendable by 90 days
mcqs.explain: Section 27 limits it to the period sought or 90 days from the effective date, with a further 90 days on request. In practice: deposit estimated tax in advance.
mcqs.topic: Procedure, special persons and effective date (ss. 25–27)

mcqs.q: Applied 45 days after becoming liable; effective date of registration is:
options: First day of the next month
mcqs.explain: Only an application within 30 days relates back to the date of liability; otherwise the date of grant applies. In practice: interest and penalty may arise for the gap.
mcqs.topic: Procedure, special persons and effective date (ss. 25–27)

mcqs.q: Which change needs the proper officer's approval?
mcqs.explain: Core fields — legal name, principal place of business and additional places, partners or directors — need approval. In practice: others are self-amended.

mcqs.q: Revocation of cancellation can be sought within:
mcqs.explain: Section 30 and Rule 23 allow 90 days, which can be extended by up to 180 days by specified authorities. In practice: file all pending returns first.

summary: Threshold ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in 4 States); ₹40 lakh for exclusive goods suppliers in most States.
Aggregate turnover: all-India under PAN incl. exempt and exports; excl. RCM inward and taxes.
s. 23: exempt-only suppliers, agriculturists, notified; s. 24: compulsory list.
Apply in 30 days; casual/non-resident 5 days before; 90-day validity.
remember: Separate registration per State; multiple per State allowed.
traps: Exempt turnover counts in aggregate turnover.

viva.model: The value of all taxable, exempt, export and inter-State supplies of persons with the same PAN across India, excluding reverse charge inward supplies and taxes.
Inter-State taxable supply of goods, casual taxable persons and persons liable under reverse charge, among others such as TDS deductors and ECOs.
From the date of liability if applied within 30 days; otherwise from the date of grant.

viva.q: Can a person hold more than one registration in a State?
viva.model: Yes, separate registrations may be obtained for each place of business in the same State.

viva.q: What must be paid on cancellation?
viva.model: An amount equal to the ITC on stock and capital goods held, or the tax on their transaction value, whichever is higher.

cases.title: Saffron Crafts
cases.case: Saffron Crafts, Jaipur, sells handmade quilts (handicraft goods) within Rajasthan and to buyers in Delhi. Turnover last year was ₹15 lakh. It plans a 7-day stall at a Goa expo and has started selling through an e-commerce site that collects TCS.

mcqs.q: Inter-State sales of handicrafts within the threshold:
options: Do not by themselves require registration
mcqs.explain: A notification exempts persons making inter-State supplies of handicraft goods from compulsory registration up to the threshold. In practice: an e-way bill may still be needed.
mcqs.topic: Persons not liable (s. 23) and compulsory registration (s. 24)

mcqs.q: If Saffron also sold machine-made carpets (not handicrafts) at the Goa stall, it must:
options: Register as a casual taxable person in Goa
Register as a non-resident taxable person
mcqs.explain: Occasional taxable supply in a State with no fixed place of business makes it a casual taxable person, who must register regardless of turnover (the handicraft relief would not cover carpets that are not handicrafts). In practice: apply 5 days before the expo.
mcqs.topic: Procedure, special persons and effective date (ss. 25–27)

mcqs.q: Sales through an ECO collecting TCS:
mcqs.explain: Section 24 covers persons supplying through ECOs that collect TCS, except notified small sellers meeting conditions. In practice: check the current notification.
mcqs.topic: Persons not liable (s. 23) and compulsory registration (s. 24)

mcqs.q: Saffron's registration threshold for goods in Rajasthan:
mcqs.explain: Rajasthan applies the ₹40 lakh limit for exclusive goods suppliers. In practice: services would bring it to ₹20 lakh.
